facts.statement: The genus Eonessa was first described by Alexander Wetmore in May 1938.
facts.quote: It was first described by Alexander Wetmore in the Journal of Paleontology in May 1938.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected on August 26, 1936, from the Myton Pocket in Duchesne County, Utah, USA.
facts.quote: The holotype was collected on 26 August 1936, from the Myton Pocket, Duchesne County, Utah, USA.

facts.statement: Eonessa lived during the Middle Eocene, approximately 46 to 42 million years ago.
facts.quote: The quarry is on the Myton Member of the Uinta Formation and dates to the Middle Eocene, around 46-42 million years ago.

facts.statement: In 1978, Storrs Olson and Alan Feduccia removed Eonessa from the family Anatidae after restudying the holotype.
facts.quote: Restudy of the holotype specimen in 1978 by Storrs Olson and Alan Feduccia resulted in the removal of Eonessa from Anatidae.

facts.statement: Olson and Feduccia classified Eonessa as Aves incertae sedis, suggesting it might belong to the order Gruiformes.
facts.quote: Olson and Feduccia placed the genus as Aves incertae sedis noting it was possibly a member of the polymorphic order Gruiformes.

facts.statement: The only known specimen is a partial wing measuring 13 cm (5 inches) in length.
facts.quote: the holotype and only known specimen is a 13 cm (5 in) long partial wing, consisting of metacarpals down to the partial humerus.

facts.statement: The bones of the holotype were found articulated but were badly crushed during fossilization.
facts.quote: Though found articulated, the bones were badly crushed during fossilization.

facts.statement: After matrix removal in the 1970s, the bones were found to be very slender with little diagnostic detail and no similarity to modern Anatidae.
facts.quote: The bones, after further matrix removal in the 1970s, are very slender and with little diagnostic detail and little to no similarity to modern Anatidae members.

facts.statement: Eonessa belongs to the parent group Eonessinae.
Eonessa is classified within the family Anatidae.
The time range for Eonessa spans from the Lutetian to the Bartonian stages, between 45.9 and 39.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Bartonian (45.9 to 39.7 million years ago)
